content:
I think the audience for the following is mostly @𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒, @Marc Huisinga, @Julian Berman, and @Willem vanhulle, but some other folks in this channel might be interested.

I am using and have developed a Python library lspleanklib and LSP server Lspleank that provides some of the functionality that @Julian Berman has implemented inside lean.nvim. Thank you Julian, lean.nvim has been a very useful example! In my case, functionality is implemented inside a "standardized" LSP server rather than an editor plugin.

Part of this "LSP standardization" is "Leank-flavor LSP" which I have documented at a brief technical level at: <https://github.com/castedo/lspleanklib/blob/main/docs/leank-lsp.md> and <https://gitlab.com/castedo/lspleanklib/-/blob/main/docs/leank-lsp.md> Use which ever git platform you hate less :smile:.

If folks would like me to turn this into an RFC in some particular format, let me know.

Comments, questions, concerns, feedback, etc... are welcome.

I happily code as lone wolf but I'm also happy to communicate and coordinate development plans with others. In particular, there are many opportunities for lake serve or another FRO project to obsolete various parts of lspleanklib. For example, lake serve could obsolete and eliminate the need for the CLI utility and functionality of lakelspout from lspleanklib.

Lspleank is a stepping stone to a more ambitious Webleank.

Nice! I always hesitate to provide first-take feedback before having time to spend dedicated to what you've written and offering more educated feedback, but time is shorter than ever these days it seems, so maybe first-take is better than nothing...
In that spirit: I think what would be useful in my opinion is not really that doc as you have it, but a list of "things needed beyond LSP that you are adding or solving for etc ...".

Right now I see only one of those in that doc in a first scan, you saying you're adding support for rootUri. I don't know why Lake only supports cwd (in fact I didn't know it did so at all until around a year ago when nvim-lspconfig was deprecated and I learned nvim-lspconfig always set cwd and I'd never noticed). But what would be useful IMHO is a list of things (behaviors) you add or modify, not which LSP methods you respond to. Then after that it will be useful to know which of those are explicitly known and not followed for one reason or another in core lean.

But I think as-is it's hard to tell what is added at a functional level, and if I read right, it says what's lost (things like inlayHint) and that means it's hard to know why that's worth losing.

Julian Berman said:

but a list of "things needed beyond LSP that you are adding or solving for etc ...".

I'm thinking perhaps an efficient way for me to do this is to use either github/gitlab issues/items. I don't see you on gitlab so I'm assuming you prefer using GitHub (as I image most people do). So I could start recording ideas/plans as github enhancements. Is this kind of along the lines you are thinking?

Julian Berman said:

you saying you're adding support for rootUri

Just to clarify, everything in that tech reference page is implemented and currently in the latest version deployed, v0.3.

Julian Berman said:

a list of things (behaviors) you add or modify, not which LSP methods you respond to. Then after that it will be useful to know which of those are explicitly known and not followed for one reason or another in core lean.

OK, I'll trying documenting something along these lines. Perhaps with an emphasis on interoperability scenarios with editors and user experiences.

Julian Berman said:

it says what's lost (things like inlayHint) and that means it's hard to know why that's worth losing

Makes sense. I'll plan on documenting this angle better. As a quick detail to share regarding inlayHint, here's a GH issue on this that has been marked P-low https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/7488 and causes problems apparently in Helix https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/pull/12735#issuecomment-4098539158

On the topic of whether it's worth losing non-standard LSP features that violate the LSP protocol, my current thinking is that for A) the main objectives of FRO staff, it is not worth it. But for B) lspleanklib, it is worth it. A) has a priority to work really well with VS Code and B) lspleanklib has a priority to work with LSP-compatible editors without Lean-specific LSP adjustments.
And I'm sure there are other differences in priority between the FRO and myself. :sweat_smile:

Castedo Ellerman said:

I'm thinking perhaps an efficient way for me to do this is to use either github/gitlab issues/items. I don't see you on gitlab so I'm assuming you prefer using GitHub (as I image most people do). So I could start recording ideas/plans as github enhancements. Is this kind of along the lines you are thinking?

I don't recommend focusing on where it's communicated. If or when there's a suggestion for upstream core lean then it matters that it's communicated in a form that follows core lean's mechanisms, but if you're sharing a doc I don't think anyone will care which of these it is maintained in.

Castedo Ellerman said:

Just to clarify, everything in that tech reference page is implemented and currently in the latest version deployed, v0.3.

I got that! Sorry, I used the present tense not in the sense of "you its implementer are in the middle of adding support", just in the looser sense of "a user using your project is using a thing which adds..." but language is hard

But yeah I think the broader point that focusing on what you're adding and removing is the important bit. That will at least make it clear what this is!
